title: Inclusionary zoning adopted for transit station areas
subtitle: Official Plan draft review, Sugarbush South missing middle housing, affordable housing tax exemption, Denholm Pond upgrades and online heritage notices.
overview: Council adopted Official Plan Amendment 50 and Zoning By-law Amendment Z-23-15, introducing inclusionary zoning in protected major transit station areas {{vote:m12}}. Developers in these areas will have to set aside a share of new units as affordable, starting at low rates and rising over time. A late amendment directs staff to bring back revised set-aside rates if the first phase of the Official Plan review is not approved in fall 2024 {{vote:m11}}.

Council also received draft Official Plan policy updates and directed staff to consult the public over the summer and fall {{vote:m8}}. Staff will engage the Sugarbush South neighbourhood on a missing middle housing plan {{vote:m9}}. Council adopted a by-law giving a property tax exemption for affordable housing, which follows the Region's program {{vote:m10}}.

Other decisions covered stormwater upgrades at Denholm Pond, publishing heritage notices on the City's website instead of a newspaper, the 2023 financial statements, a servicing agreement for a King Street North development in Woolwich, and the Rink in the Park lease. Council met in closed session earlier in the day, and the minutes record no public decisions from it. Under new business, the Mayor reported on a Regional special meeting with the Association of Municipalities of Ontario about municipal funding.

decisions.detail: Council adopted Official Plan Amendment 50 and Zoning By-law Amendment Z-23-15, directed an agreement with the Region on administration, and required monitoring reports by the end of 2024, 2026, 2028 and 2030.
If Official Plan Phase One is not approved in fall 2024, staff must bring forward revised inclusionary zoning set-aside rates for Council to consider.
Council received the draft policy updates for Chapters 3, 10 and 12 for information and directed staff to consult and return with a final draft.
Council received the Housing Accelerator Fund corridor report and directed staff to engage the neighbourhood and return with a missing middle housing plan.
Council adopted a by-law for a property tax exemption for affordable housing, supporting the Region's program and authorizing the Treasurer to negotiate agreements.
Council endorsed the Environmental Assessment, started the 30-day public review, and released $717,000 from the Stormwater Reserve.
Council approved publishing Ontario Heritage Act notices on the City's website to meet newspaper notice requirements.
Council authorized agreements letting a development at 713-725 King Street North in Woolwich connect to municipal services on Colby Court.

debate: Staff said inclusionary zoning is one tool among several and a modest one. They said it would produce a steady yearly supply of affordable units and could run without competing for City funds.

Development industry delegates asked for more consultation and for the policy to be deferred or phased until the Official Plan review is complete. They raised market uncertainty, how stations are classed as prime, established or emerging, and the cost being passed on to buyers of other units in a building. One delegate argued for higher heights to offset costs.

Delegates also raised concern that eligibility is checked only when a tenant moves in. Staff replied that the Residential Tenancies Act limits what can be done afterward. One councillor cautioned against implying that people needing affordable housing would abuse the system.
Residents and renters spoke in support, saying the supply is small but needed. They also asked for other measures such as removing parking minimums and allowing more density.

In the Official Plan discussion, councillors asked for in-person, ward-specific consultation on land use maps. They also asked for a definition of neighbourhood character, clearer plain-language terms, and attention to trees, green space and noise. Staff said natural heritage and parks policies would come in a later phase.
